items.stem: What are track and field events? Which of these also belong to the category of team sports?
items.answer: Track and field events are comprised with running events and field events. All running events are held in the track and are categorised as short distance, middle distance and long distance running, race walk, hurdles and steeplechase events. Field events are categorised as throwing and jumping events. Of these, the relay races also belong to the category of team sports - the common relays being the 4x100 meter and the 4x400 meter - because relay races are the only track events in which a team of runners directly competes against other teams.
grounding: Track and field events are comprised with running events and field events.
All running events are held in the track and categorised as short distance, middle distance and long distance running, race walk, hurdles and steeplechase events.
Field events are categorised as, throwing and jumping events.
Relay races are the only track events in which a team of runners directly compete against other teams.
Common relay races are the 4x100 meter and the 4x400 meter.

items.stem: What are the main track rules?
items.answer: The rules of track events are formulated by the International Association of Athletics Federation (IAAF), and the key rules relate to three phases - starting, running and finishing. Starting: the start of a race is marked 5 cm wide by a white line, and in all races that are not run in lanes the start line must be curved so that all the athletes run the same distance upto the finish. Starting blocks shall be used for all races up to and including 400 meter, including the first lap of the 4x100 and 4x400, and shall not be used for any other race; any sprinter with a false start is considered disqualified. Running: in all races that are run in lanes the athletes have to keep themselves in their allocated lanes from start to finish, and an athlete who leaves the track or steps on the line demarking the track is disqualified, as is any athlete found intentionally obstructing the path of another runner. Finishing: the finish of a race is marked by a white line 5 cm wide, and competitors are placed in the order in which any part of their torso reaches the vertical plane of the nearer edge of the finish line. The measurement of time is taken from the flash or the smoke of the gun to the finishing touch and is recorded in 1/100th of a second if taken manually.
grounding: The rules of track events, as observed in most international athletics competitions, are formulated by the International Association of Athletics Federation (IAAF).
Key rules of track events relate to three phases - starting, running and finishing.
The start of a race is marked 5 cm wide by a white line.
In all races, that are not run in lanes, the start line must be curved, so that all the athletes run the same distance upto the finish.
Starting blocks shall be used for all races up to and including 400 meter (including the first lap of the 4x100 and 4x400) and shall not be used for any other race.
Any sprinter with a false start is considered disqualified.
In all races that are run in lanes, athletes have keep themselves their allocated lanes from start to finish.
If an athlete leaves the track or steps on the line demarking the track, this will be considered disqualified.
Any athlete found intentionally obstructing the path of another runner is also disqualified from the race.
The finish of a race is marked by a white line 5 cm wide.

Competitors are placed in the order in which any part of their torso (as distinguished from the head, neck, arms, legs, hands or feet) reaches the vertical plane of the nearer edge of the finish line.
The measurement of time shall be taken from the flash or the smoke of the gun to the finishing touch, which shall be recorded in 1/100th of a second if taken manually.

items.stem: Describe the major rules that are observed in long jump.
items.answer: The take-off has to be made from a 20 cm wide board one meter away from a pit, the athletes sprinting along a length of track to the take off board and the sandpit. Horizontal jumps such as the long jump must be initiated from behind the line: if any part of the runner's foot goes past the takeoff board, the jumper is considered for a foul and does not receive score for that round. Distance is measured from the end of the takeoff board to the nearest mark made by the jumper on the pit. The best eight competitors have a maximum of six rounds.
grounding: The take-off has to be made from a 20 cm wide board one meter away from a pit.
Athletes sprint along a length of track to a take off board and a sandpit.
If any part of the runner's foot goes past the takeoff board, the jumper is considered for a foul and does not receive score for that round.
Distance is measured from the end of the takeoff board to the nearest mark made by the jumper on the pit.
Best eight competitors have a maximum of six rounds.
Horizontal jumps (long jump and triple jump) must be initiated from behind a line.

items.stem: Describe the special features of triple jump and high jump.
items.answer: Triple jump: similar to the long jump, it takes place on a field heading towards a sandpit and is termed the 'hop-step and jump' - the competitor dashes down the runway and, leaping from a takeoff board, first hops, then takes a step and then jumps into the pit; the event is scored identically to the long jump. High jump: competitors combine speed, to generate lift, with jumping technique. Jumpers may approach the bar from either side and land on a large, generally inflated cushion, and in between they must clear the 4-meter-long bar without knocking it off its supports. An athlete is allowed a maximum of three trials of each height, and competitors are eliminated after missing three consecutive jumps in a particular height.
grounding: Similar to the long jump, the triple jump takes place on a field heading towards a sandpit.
This event is termed as the "hop-step and jump."
The event begins like a long jump, with competitor dashing down the runway and leaping from a takeoff board they first hop then take a step and then jump into the pit.
The event is scored identically to the long jump.
In high jump event, competitors combined speed, to generate lift, with jumping technique.
Jumpers may approach the bar from either-side, and land on a large, generally inflated cushion.
In between, they must clear the 4-meter-long bar without knocking it off its supports.
An athlete is allowed a maximum of three trials of each height.
Competitors are eliminated after missing (failing) three consecutive jumps in a particular height.

items.stem: Discuss the specific rules for shot put and discus throw.
items.answer: Shot put: the athletes put a metal ball through the air for maximum distance; for male athletes the metal ball weights 7.26 kg and for female athletes the weight is 4 kg. The athlete must stay in a circle of 2.135 m (7 ft) diameter until the shot has landed after the throw, holds the shot close to the neck in one hand, and the put must be made from the shoulder with one arm only, the shot never being brought behind the shoulder. Discus: the athlete stands inside a throwing circle of 2.5 mt diameter and throws a disc, a round plate made of wood and metal, which weighs 2 Kg for men and 1 Kg for women. As per technique he or she turns around one and a half times and throws the disc as far as possible. The athlete must remain in the circle and the feet cannot leave this area before the discus lands; even afterwards the athlete must leave the circle from the rear half of the circle, otherwise it is a fault and the throw will not be counted. For both events a throw landing on the line, on the edge of the sector, is a foul.
grounding: In putting the shot event the athletes put a metal ball through the air for maximum distance.
For male athletes, the metal ball weights 7.26 kg and for female athletes the weight is 4 kg.
The athlete must stay in a circle of 2.135 m (7 ft) diameter until the shot has landed after throw.
The put must be made from the shoulder with one arm only, and the shot must not be brought behind the shoulder.
In shot put the athlete holds the shot close to their neck in one hand.
In the discus event the athlete stands inside a throwing circle of 2.5 mt
The disc is a round plate made of wood and metal and weighs 2 Kg for men and 1 Kg for women.
As per technique he/she turns around one and a half times and throws the disc as far as he or she can.
When throwing the discus, the athlete must remain in circle.
The feet of the athlete cannot leave this area before the discus lands.
Even afterwards the athlete must leave the circle from rear half of the circle.
Otherwise it is a fault and the throw will not be counted.
A throw landing on the line, on the edge of sector, is a foul.

items.stem: How do you break a tie in high jump?
items.answer: The bar does not shift to a lower height except to break a tie for first place or a qualifying position. If those critical positions are still tied after applying the tiebreakers, all tied competitors will take a fourth jump at the last height. If they still miss, the bar will go down one increment where they will again jump, and this process will continue until the tie is broken.
grounding: The bar does not shift to a lower height except to break a tie for first place or a qualifying position.

This process will continue until the tie is broken.

items.answer: In the high jump the competitor combines speed, to generate lift, with jumping technique. The athlete has a short run up and then takes off from near one foot to jump over a horizontal bar and falls back onto a cushioned landing area, and jumpers may approach the bar from either side, landing on a large, generally inflated cushion. The bar is originally set at a low height, at which competitors may choose to jump or pass to another height, and it is raised to a predetermined height after each round; each competitor who either clears or passes a height advances to the next round, and they are ranked according to the height they clear. The modern technique of high jump is known as the 'Fosbury Flop'.
grounding: In high jump event, competitors combined speed, to generate lift, with jumping technique.

Each competitor who either clears or passes a height advances to the next round.
They are ranked according to the height they clear.

items.answer: Relay races are the only track events in which a team of runners directly competes against other teams, and the common relay races are the 4x100 meter and the 4x400 meter. The exchange of baton takes place within a specified area of the track called the baton exchange zone, and a team that fails to complete the baton exchange within an area of 20 meters is considered disqualified, as is a team whose runners have deliberately created hurdle for the other competitors. The 4x100 meter event is run strictly within the same lane on the track, which means that the team collectively runs one complete circuit of the track. Teams in a 4x400 meter event remain in their own lane until the runner of the second leg passes the first bend, at which point runners can leave their lanes and head towards the inner-most part of the circuit; for the second and third baton change-overs the leading team takes the inner lanes while team mates of the slower teams must await the baton on outer lanes.
grounding: Relay races are the only track events in which a team of runners directly compete against other teams.
Common relay races are the 4x100 meter and the 4x400 meter.

Teams may be disqualified if the team fails to complete the baton exchange within an area of 20 meters, the team is considered as disqualified.
A team may also be disqualified if its runners have deliberately created hurdle for the other competitors.
The 4x100 meter event is run strictly within the same lane on the track. It means that the team collectively runs one complete circuit of the track.
Teams in a 4x400 meter event remain in
their own lane until the runner of the second leg passes the first bend, at which point runners can leave their lanes and head towards the inner-most part of the circuit.
For the second and third baton change-overs, team mates must align themselves in respect of their team position.
The leading team takes the inner lanes while team mates of the slower teams must await the baton on outer lanes.

items.stem: In which events does the athlete take standing position to start the race?
items.answer: The middle distance races - 800 meters and 1500 meters - are started from a standing start position, in the lanes along a curved starting line or in staggered lanes. Starting blocks are used only for races up to and including 400 meter and shall not be used for any other race, so the longer races are also started standing, the starter's command for a standing start being 'on your mark'.
grounding: The middle distance races are of 800 meters and 1500 meters.
Runners start the race from a standing start position in the lanes along a curved starting line or in staggered lanes.
Starting blocks shall be used for all races up to and including 400 meter (including the first lap of the 4x100 and 4x400) and shall not be used for any other race.
In most international competitions, the command of the starter is "on your marks" and "set" for crouch start and "on your mark" for standing start.
